citations.inTextDetails: Official AAS style is author-year: "References should be cited in text by the last name of the author(s) and the date of publication." Current style (references page + AASTeX v7) adds first initials: single author "(G. E. Hale 1929)" — "the first initial(s) and last name of the author and the year of publication, with no comma before the date"; two authors joined by an ampersand "(G. B. Press & W. H. Rybicki 1992)"; three or more authors: first author + "et al." + date "(A. A. Goodman et al. 2003)". In LaTeX, natbib \citep/\citet with the latest aasjournal.bst is required; the .bst "automatically produces inline citations with first author initials." No stated rules for collating numeric ranges (not applicable to author-year).
citations.maxReferences: None stated for ApJ, ApJL, AJ, ApJS. Exception: Research Notes of the AAS — references count toward the total "1,500 words or fewer" limit.
citations.referenceListFormat: Alphabetical by last name of first author; multiple entries for the same author(s) ordered chronologically; same authors + same year distinguished with lowercase suffixes ("2025a", "2025b"); entries cited as "et al." are "grouped together and last, as if the fourth author started with 'z'". Author truncation: for articles with more than five authors, "the last name and initials of the first three authors only should be listed, followed by a comma and 'et al.'" Journal abbreviations: use ADS bibliographic codes "Except in rare instances (e.g., Icarus)". DOI policy: "References in accepted manuscripts should include digital object identifiers (DOI) if available. DOIs should be written in full with either a 'doi:' or an 'https://doi.org/' prefix." Example journal entry: "Martín, E. L., Rebolo, R., & Zapatero Osorio, M. R. 1996, ApJ, 469, 706, doi:10.1086/177817". Preprints citable "only for manuscripts not yet published" (example: "Crida, A., Baruteau, C., Gonzalez, J.-F., et al. 2025, arXiv e-prints, arXiv:2508.07859, doi: 10.48550/arXiv.2508.07859"). Software/data: cite both the canonical paper and a DOI to the artifact where possible; repository pattern "{author} {year}, {title}, {version}, {publisher}, {prefix}:{identifier}" (example: "Corrales, L. 2015, dust: ..., v1.0, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.15991"). All sources cited in text and tables (including online-only tables) must appear in the reference list.

figures.widths: Not stated in mm or column presets on the official Graphics Guide. Implied sizing: raster figures must have "at minimum 1000 pixels of horizontal resolution" at 300 DPI on the final PDF page (~85 mm / single column equivalent). Interactive figures: "The width of the current viewport in the article landing page for HTML interactive graphics is 650 pixels." In AASTeX, \plotone/\plottwo scale figures "so that the horizontal dimension fits the width of the body text"; \gridline/\fig accept fractional widths (e.g., 0.33\textwidth).
figures.fonts: "Common fonts, such as Times, Helvetica, or Symbol"; "A minimum of 6 pt. font size is acceptable" at final size. No maximum stated.
figures.lineWeights: "Lines in figures should be at minimum 0.5 points." No maximum stated.
figures.color: "The use of color as the only distinguishing delimiter in a figure should be generally avoided": colored lines must also use different line styles, colored symbols varied in shape, colored histograms different hatching or weights. Colorblind-check tools (Color Oracle) and colorblind-safe palettes (viridis, cube-helix) are recommended. RGB vs CMYK requirement: not stated on the Graphics Guide.
figures.formats: Vector EPS or PDF preferred; "Scalar (PNG, JPG, TIFF) formats are also acceptable" at "minimum 300 DPI on the final PDF page." Images must not be used for tables or equations.
figures.panelLabels: Only stated rule: "If a figure is part of a lettered, multipart figure, place the letter within the box around the figure, not outside of it." Case/bold/punctuation convention: not stated (AAS practice in templates is lowercase (a), (b), but the official page does not mandate this).
figures.other: Journal-specific pages on journals.aas.org are the sole authority; no Nature-family or AAAS umbrella guidelines apply to ApJ/AAS Journals. IOP Publishing (production partner) defers to journals.aas.org for author instructions.

manuscript.titleLimit: Full title: no limit stated. Short title / running head: "not more than 44 characters."
manuscript.abstractLimit: "Not more than 250 words" (unstructured) for ApJ, ApJL, and other main AAS journals; Research Notes of the AAS: 150-word limit. AASTeX v7 enforces "250 words" / "150 for RNAAS."
manuscript.lengthLimits: ApJ (regular articles): no length, figure-count, or reference-count limit stated. ApJ Letters: main text "no more than 3500 words (not including acknowledgments, appendices or other supplementary material)"; "no more than 5 combined figures (each limited to 9 panels) and tables, e.g. 3 figures and 2 tables"; these limits "are no longer intended to be compulsory" — manuscripts exceeding them "can be considered at the discretion of the Scientific Editor." Research Notes: "1,500 words or fewer" total (references and captions count; abstract's 150 words reserved within it), max "a single figure or table (but not both)."
manuscript.requiredSections: Manuscripts consist of: title page, abstract, text (figures/tables integrated — "it is no longer required to place figures and tables at the ends of manuscripts"), acknowledgments, appendices, references. Per the AASTeX v7 guide, acknowledgments, author contributions, facilities, and software sections go "after the main body of text but before the bibliography"; each author needs an \email command. A dedicated "Data Availability" section is not stated as required; data/software citation rules are on the References and Data Guide pages instead.
manuscript.submissionFormat: AASTeX (most recent version, currently v7) or Microsoft Word (.doc/.docx); Overleaf accepted. Word template: "Courier New serif font with a 10 point size and 1.5 line spacing" (Times New Roman 12pt or Calibri 12pt also allowed). Line numbers are REQUIRED for submission and revision: AASTeX v6+ via the linenumbers style option, other LaTeX via lineno.sty (exception: Research Notes — "Do not use line numbers"). AASTeX style options include manuscript ("12 point font in a double spaced, single column style") — double spacing per se is delivered via that option rather than stated as a standalone rule. Graphics submitted as vector EPS/PDF or raster JPG/PNG/TIFF at 300 DPI minimum; "Authors must not use images for tables or equations."

journal: The Astrophysical Journal (ApJ) / AAS Journals (ApJ, ApJL, AJ, ApJS, PSJ, RNAAS)

sources.what: Official manuscript preparation guidelines: file types, Word template fonts/spacing, line-number requirement, running head 44-character limit, 250-word abstract, section order, in-text author-year citation rule

Official reference/citation instructions: in-text author-year with initials, ampersand and et al. rules, alphabetization, 3-authors-then-et-al. truncation for >5 authors, ADS journal abbreviations, DOI policy, preprint/software/dataset citation formats with verbatim examples

Official graphics guide: EPS/PDF vector preferred, 300 DPI / 1000 px minimum for raster, 6 pt minimum font, 0.5 pt minimum line weight, color-not-sole-delimiter rule, colorblind-safe palette recommendations, panel-letter placement, 650 px interactive viewport
ApJ Letters requirements: 3500-word main text, 250-word abstract, 5 combined figures+tables (9 panels max each), limits discretionary with Scientific Editor
Research Notes of the AAS: 1,500-word total limit, 150-word abstract, single figure or table, references count toward limit, no line numbers

AASTeX v7 author guide: style options (default 10pt single-spaced; manuscript 12pt double-spaced), \plotone/\gridline figure sizing, aasjournal.bst + natbib citation machinery, section ordering (acknowledgments/facilities/software before bibliography)

confidence_notes: All numbers above were found on official journals.aas.org pages (freely accessible, no paywall) and are quoted verbatim where possible. Explicitly NOT stated on official pages (reported as such rather than invented): figure column widths in mm, RGB vs CMYK requirement, maximum line weight, full-title word limit, reference-count limits for ApJ/ApJL, panel-label case/punctuation convention, and a required Data Availability section. Umbrella-guideline note: no Nature-family or AAAS (Science) umbrella rules apply — ApJ is published by the American Astronomical Society with IOP Publishing as production partner, and journals.aas.org is the sole authoritative source for author instructions; IOP-hosted journal pages defer to it. The ApJL "5-6 page limit" that appears in web search summaries comes from third-party sites (manusights.com), not the official page, and was excluded; the official ApJL page states word/figure limits only and notes they are no longer compulsory. The AASTeX v7 guide page did not surface the linenumbers option in the fetched extract, but the manuscript-preparation page explicitly requires line numbers via "the linenumbers style option" (AASTeX v6+) or lineno.sty.

journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS) — Royal Astronomical Society / Oxford University Press

sources.what: Official 'Instructions to Authors' page (primary source for everything below; internal sections cited: 1.2 article types, 2.1 LaTeX, 2.3 abstract/keywords/structure, 2.4 colour/accessibility, 2.9 data availability, 3.6 initial submission, 4.2 revisions, 4.3 accepted 'First Look' files, 5.3 figure/graphics preparation, 6.1 layout/figures, 6.2 spelling/maths style, 6.3 references, 6.7 units)
Official MNRAS LaTeX class (mnras.cls) location, as linked from the Instructions to Authors page
Journal home page (Oxford Academic)

citations.inTextDetails: Harvard author-year style (Section 6.3). Note: the current official page's examples include first initials in in-text citations. Verbatim: 'For one author, use either the form (J. Brown 1999) or e.g. the observations of J. Brown (1999)…, as appropriate for the context. For two authors, use an ampersand: J. Brown & P. Jones (1991). For three authors, give all three names at first mention, e.g. (J. Brown, P. Jones & A. Smith 1994), but use first author et al. (in roman, not italic) thereafter, e.g. (J. Brown et al. 1994). For more than three authors, use the first author et al., e.g. (J. Brown et al. 1994).' Multiple papers by same author collate as '(J. Brown 1992, 1995)'; same-year papers as 'A. Smith et al. (2000a,b)'; several citations in one bracket are separated by semicolons, e.g. '(A. Smith et al. 1990; J. Brown et al. 1995)'. Private communications or papers in preparation are cited in the text only ('Smith (in preparation) shows that…') and omitted from the reference list.
citations.referenceListFormat: Alphabetical by surname; no bold or italic, no commas after surnames, no ampersand between the final two names. Journal-article pattern (verbatim example): 'Eke V., Cole S., Frenk C.S., 1996, MNRAS, 282, 263'. Book example: 'Peebles P. J. E., 1980, The Large-Scale Structure of the Universe. Princeton Univ. Press, Princeton, NJ'. Author truncation rule (verbatim): 'List all of the authors if there are eight or fewer, otherwise give just the first author followed by et al.' — e.g. 'Pounds K. A. et al., 1993, MNRAS, 260, 77'. Preprints: 'Smith P. et al., 2013, preprint (arXiv:0123.45678)'. Software/data: full citation in reference list when in an online source; ASCL example 'Brown J., 2015, Astrophysics Source Code Library, record ascl:1234.567'. Journal abbreviations: a simplified list of ~20 frequent journals is given (A&A, ApJ, AJ, MNRAS, Nature, Science, PASP, PASJ, A&ARv, ApJS, ARA&A, BAAS, QJRAS, Rev. Mex. Astron. Astrofis., …); 'For journals not on this list, use the IAU standard abbreviations.' DOI policy: no requirement to print DOIs is stated; the page warns that online links are generated from reference details ('If the reference details are wrong then the links will fail'), so details must be accurate.
citations.maxReferences: None stated. The page only advises: 'Long lists of citations…should be avoided, unless the articles cited are directly relevant.'

figures.widths: Single column: 'approx. 80 mm wide, or 3.15 inches' (Section 5.3). No full-text-width (two-column) figure dimension is stated on the page.
figures.fonts: 'use a common font like Times, Arial or Helvetica for labelling'; 'Axis labelling, lettering and any plotting symbols should be sized appropriately for the figure and its likely final size of around font size 8 point.' All fonts (and logos) must be embedded in the figure file. No stated maximum size.
figures.lineWeights: 'the weight should not be less than 0.3 pt at final size'; line thickness must 'withstand a possibly significant reduction in size'. No maximum stated.
figures.color: Accessibility (Section 2.4): 'Where possible, please ensure that your figures are colour-blind friendly. The use of red and green in the same figure is particularly problematic for some readers.' Recommended tools: ColorBrewer and Color Oracle. No RGB-vs-CMYK requirement stated; no colour charges stated (journal is fully Open Access). Related: colouring/shading of table cells 'cannot be supported in the web version' — use bold text or superscript symbols instead.
figures.formats: Preferred: Encapsulated PostScript (EPS); 'PDF and TIFF (Tagged Image File Format) files can also be used' (Section 5.3). EPS: include PC preview/header, crop tightly with minimal white space, embed all fonts/logos. Resolution for TIFF at final size: '300 pixels per inch (ppi) for grey-scale/half-tone figures (e.g. photographs), and 800 ppi for combined line/tone figures' — worked example: an 80 mm (3.15 in) column figure needs ≥945 px (photo) or ~2500 px (line/tone). Bitmapped elements inside vector files: 'effective resolution (i.e. at final printing) of 400 dpi or greater'. Name files clearly (e.g. 'fig6.eps' for Fig. 6); no long/complicated filenames. Initial submission is a single file ≤10 MB with figures included; supplementary material ≤350 MB combined, published exactly as supplied.
figures.panelLabels: 'Where a figure has several parts, labels (a), (b) etc. should be added as appropriate' — i.e. lowercase letters in parentheses. All such labels must be embedded in the graphics file itself: 'please do not use LaTeX code to include these labels as the figures are processed entirely separately from the LaTeX code.' (Section 6.1)
figures.other: Plots 'should have borders on all sides and fiducial marks on every border. Axes should be labelled and include the units.' Refer to figures/tables as 'Fig. 1' and 'Table 1' (but lowercase 'fig. 1' / 'table 1' when citing another paper's). Every figure/table needs a number and caption and must be cited in the text in numerical order. Figures 'should be placed at logical points in the text (i.e. not all at the end).'

manuscript.titleLimit: No numeric limit stated. 'Titles should be informative, and obscure acronyms should be avoided'; the editor may request removal of title content 'intended mainly or solely to attract attention'. A running head (short form of title) is used; no character limit is stated on this page.
manuscript.abstractLimit: Unstructured, single paragraph. Papers: 'normally of not more than 250 words'. Letters: not more than 200 words. Corrections have no abstract. Abstract is followed by 'between one and six key words' chosen from the MNRAS key words list (Section 2.3).
manuscript.lengthLimits: Papers: 'There are no page limits, but it is important for Papers to be concise.' Letters: 'must not exceed five pages in length. The title, author list, affiliations, abstract, keywords, data availability statement, acknowledgements and references are not included in the page limit.' No figure-count limits stated. Initial-submission file ≤10 MB; supplementary material ≤350 MB combined.
manuscript.requiredSections: Title page (title, authors, affiliations, correspondence); Abstract; Key words (1–6 from official list); numbered sections/subsections with Introduction first and Conclusions last; numbered equations; numbered, captioned figures/tables cited in order; then un-numbered endmatter in this order: Acknowledgements, Data Availability, References, with any Appendices at the end (Section 6.1). A Data Availability Statement is mandatory: 'The inclusion of a Data Availability Statement is a requirement for articles published in MNRAS' and it 'should be included in the endmatter of your article (after the Acknowledgements) under the heading Data availability' (Section 2.9).
manuscript.submissionFormat: LaTeX with the official mnras class is recommended (class files and documentation on CTAN: ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/mnras); Overleaf template is available and revisions may be submitted directly from Overleaf. Layout: 'Papers should be formatted with two columns (except the abstract) and single line spaced' — i.e. NOT double-spaced; line numbers are not mentioned/required on the official page. Initial submission: a single file containing all figures and tables, in 'PDF, PS, Word, RTF or plain text', ≤10 MB (Section 3.6). Revisions: changes 'highlighted (e.g. in bold or colour)' (4.2). After acceptance ('First Look'): supply source files — .tex, .eps, .bib etc. (LaTeX) or .doc/.docx plus figure files (Word) — combined into a .zip or .tar.gz archive (4.3). Style: British English spellings ('centre not center, sulphur not sulfur'; 'acknowledgements, artefact, best-fitting, disc, haloes, time-scale'); SI units plus astronomy-recognized units, roman type, non-breaking space before unit ('200 keV'), 'km s−1 not km/s'; scalars italic, vectors bold italic, roman d/i/e and function names. Fully Open Access journal (CC BY licence); APCs stated: Papers £2,356 non-members, Letters £1,122 non-members, each with 20% RAS-member discount.

confidence_notes: All content above comes from the official Oxford Academic MNRAS 'Instructions to Authors' page (academic.oup.com/mnras/pages/general_instructions), extracted via WebFetch with verbatim-quote prompts; direct curl download is blocked by Cloudflare, so quotes rely on WebFetch page renderings, which were internally consistent across five independent targeted extractions. Notable and verified three times verbatim: the current page's in-text citation examples INCLUDE first initials — '(J. Brown 1999)', 'J. Brown & P. Jones (1991)' — which differs from the traditional output of the older mnras.bst BibTeX style (which prints 'Brown 1999' without initials); authors using the stock class/bst should be aware the official page now shows initials. Umbrella-guideline note: Nature-family and AAAS/Science umbrella guidelines do NOT apply to MNRAS; the journal-specific OUP page is the authoritative formatting source (RAS's ras.ac.uk editorial-policies page covers ethics/policy, not formatting, and was not needed here). Explicitly NOT stated on the official page (report as 'not stated' rather than inferred): title word/character limit, running-head character limit, full-width (two-column) figure dimension in mm, RGB vs CMYK requirement, colour figure charges, maximum number of references, maximum figure count, and any line-numbering requirement. Letters are formally published in MNRAS: Letters (academic.oup.com/mnrasl), whose instructions mirror the MNRAS page.

sources.what: Instructions for preparing an initial manuscript: manuscript format/order, title/abstract limits, supplementary materials, figure preparation (widths, fonts, line weights, color guidance, panel labels), and the full 'Science Citation Style' section with reference-list examples

Information for authors: categories of manuscripts with word/display-item/reference limits (Research Articles, Reviews, Analytical Reviews, Perspectives, Policy Forums, Letters, etc.), submission workflow, color-in-print charges

Instructions for preparing a revised manuscript: single .docx without embedded figures, figures as separate files, resolution requirements (300 dpi), accepted figure formats (PDF/EPS/AI/TIFF), equations guidance

Official 'Guide to Preparing Figures' PDF (2025) linked from the instructions pages: file formats, 300-500 dpi resolution, Arial/Helvetica labels 6-9 pt, panel letters 10 pt bold, minimum line weight 0.28 pt (~0.10 mm), RGB color mode, colorblind-accessibility guidance, column-width box (1 column = 9 cm, 2 column = 18.3 cm)

citations.inTextDetails: Citation numbers are placed within parentheses and italicized: "(18, 19) (18–20) (18, 20–22)" — i.e., commas for collation, en dashes for ranges. References and Notes are numbered in the order cited through (i) main text, (ii) text boxes, (iii) figure and table captions, (iv) reference notes and acknowledgments, and (v) supplementary materials. One single combined reference list covers main paper + supplementary materials; each reference appears only once and has a unique number (do not combine references or embed references in notes; notes may cite other references by number). Reference citations in tables use the same italic number in parentheses referring to the main list. Do not use op. cit., ibid., or et al. Personal communications may not be cited; "in press" citations are not allowed at time of publication; preprints (arXiv, bioRxiv) may be cited; any dataset with a DOI must be cited in the reference list. No citations allowed in the Abstract. (Source: instructions-preparing-initial-manuscript)
citations.referenceListFormat: Science Citation Style (from instructions-preparing-initial-manuscript). Journal-article pattern: "1. A. B. Author, C. D. Author, Example article title. Example Journal Name 55, 100–108 (2021)." Rules: author initials first (separated by a space), family names spelled in full, commas (not "and") between authors, no punctuation before suffixes (Jr., 3rd, III); full list of authors required — "Do not use ... et al. (in place of the complete list of authors' names)" (no stated truncation threshold); article titles included, followed by a period (titles display in HTML versions but not print/PDF); journal titles in italics; volume numbers in bold (if no volume, use publication year in its place); no comma before the volume number; full page range with en dash; article number instead of page range if pagination is not continuous; year in parentheses; end each listing with a period. Epub-ahead-of-print: use DOI instead of volume and page numbers. Journal-title abbreviation: not stated on the page (examples show generic italicized journal names only). Books: "G. Y. Author, Example Book Title (Publisher, 2022)."; edited books insert "Ed.,"/"Eds.,"; chapters: "in" before book title, editors after, "pp. 300–350". Preprints: arXiv as "arXiv:1111.12345 [category] (2021)" (no word "Preprint"); bioRxiv adds "[Preprint]" and the DOI preferably as URL. Datasets/software: version number, repository name, and DOI or persistent identifier preferably in URL format, e.g. "D. Author, Example dataset title, version 1, Example Repository Name (2021); https://doi.org/10.12345/ABC1234567."
citations.maxReferences: Per article type (science-information-authors): Research Articles "about 50 main-text references"; extended-format online Research Articles "up to 100 main-text references" (meta-analyses needing more than 250 total references must contact editors before submission); Reviews "up to 150 references" (less than 20% self-citation); Analytical Reviews "up to 200 references" (fewer than 20% self-citation); Perspectives "15 references maximum"; Policy Forums and Policy Articles "up to 15 references". No limit stated for other types.

figures.widths: Instructions pages (initial and revised): "The width of figures, when printed, will usually be 5.7 cm (2.24 inches or 1 column), 12.1 cm (4.76 inches or 2 columns), or 18.4 cm (7.24 inches or 3 columns). Bar graphs, simple line graphs, and gels may be reduced to a smaller width." The 2025 Guide to Preparing Figures PDF instead gives a fit box of "1 column = 21p3 picas (9 cm, or 3.6 in.)" and "2 column = 43p4 picas (18.3 cm, or 7.25 in.)" and states "Figure and legend must fit within this box" — note both are official but the numbers differ (the PDF appears to reflect the current two-column layout).
figures.fonts: Sans-serif required for figure labels: web page says "Use a sans-serif font whenever possible (Helvetica is preferred)"; the figure guide PDF says "all text should be in a sans serif typeface, preferably Arial, or Helvetica." Sizes (guide PDF): panel-part letters 10-point bold; labels 6 to 9 points; maximum of 3 type sizes per figure for typographic hierarchy. Web instructions: symbols and lettering legible after reduction — "a reduced size of about 7 points (2.5 mm) high, and not smaller than 5 points"; plot symbols "6 point minimum"; avoid wide variation in type size within a figure. Do not rasterize, flatten, or outline text (keep live/editable text). Manuscript text font (not figures): Times New Roman preferred; avoid Symbol fonts.
figures.lineWeights: Guide PDF: "At final print size, minimum line weight is 0.28 pt (~0.10 mm)." Web instructions (initial manuscript): "Line widths should be legible upon reduction (minimum of 0.5 point at the final reduced size)." No maximum stated.
figures.color: Guide PDF: full-color artwork must be provided in RGB; color may shift when converted to CMYK for print; the figure of record is the RGB online version. Accessibility: "Avoid using combinations of red and green, but if they can't be avoided, use strongly contrasting shades/tints and add shapes or textures"; the guide links to two palette checkers (safecolours.rigdenage.com/palettefiles.html and visibone.com/colorblind). Web instructions: avoid red and green together (color-deficient vision); do not use colors similar in hue to identify different parts of a figure; avoid grayscale; use white type and scale bars over darker areas; in color figures, type atop a color region should be bold face; avoid colored type; avoid light lines and screen shading (use black-and-white, hatched, cross-hatched designs). Print color charges: $650 for the first color figure and $450 for each additional color figure (information-for-authors page).
figures.formats: Initial submission: figures embedded directly in the .docx or PDF manuscript file; create as vector-based files (e.g., Adobe Illustrator); PowerPoint files not accepted; files must be readable by Adobe Photoshop or Illustrator; save images at 300 dpi for initial submission; keep Photoshop labeling on a separate editable layer. Revised submission: each figure as an individual file, in preferred order — vector illustrations/diagrams: PDF, EPS, or AI; raster illustrations/diagrams: TIFF at minimum 300 dpi; vector+raster combinations (photos/microscopy): PDF or EPS; raster photos/microscopy: TIFF. Cannot accept figures embedded in Word or PowerPoint files at revision. Resolution (revised): line art not available as vector at least 300 dpi at final size, preferably higher; grayscale and color images minimum 300 dpi at final size, higher if possible; upsampling not permitted. Guide PDF adds: photographic images 300 to 500 dpi at final print size (300 ppi = 120 pixels/cm at 100% size); embedded images within a vector file minimum 300 ppi; convert ChemDraw/CorelDraw/Inkscape/Canvas output to pdf, eps, or ps; save R graphs as vector SVG; linked images must be embedded; do not flatten layers or transparencies; keep an archive of original images at highest resolution.
figures.panelLabels: "Use capital letters for part labels in multipart figures – A, B, C, etc. These should be 10 pt and bold in the final figure. When possible, place part labels in the upper left corner of each figure part; if a part is an image, set labels inside the perimeter." In captions, "Distinct figure panels should be labeled with uppercase letters (A, B, etc.) and should each be described in order within the caption." Avoid subpart labels; if unavoidable use lowercase letters (a, b, c), prime symbols, or lowercase Roman numerals (i, ii, iii); numbers (1, 2, 3) only for a time sequence of images. (No punctuation after the letter is shown in the examples.)
figures.other: Figure captions: single-spaced, numerical order; short bold-face title as first line; no caption longer than 200 words; figure title belongs in the caption, not in the figure. Layout: maximize space given to data, avoid wasted white space and clutter; panels set close together, common axis labels not repeated; scales/axes should not extend beyond data range; use scale bars instead of/in addition to magnifications; no minor tick marks or grid lines; solid symbols preferred; capitalize only the first letter of labels; SI units in parentheses, e.g. Pressure (MPa); variables italic or plain Greek; leading zeros on decimals (0.3, 0.55); "s" and "min." abbreviations, hours not abbreviated; lines/spaces must indicate borders when figures are assembled from multiple gels/micrographs; sequences ~130 characters/line at full page width, ~84 at two columns. Image-integrity policy: linear contrast/brightness/color adjustments must apply to the whole image; nonlinear adjustments must be stated in the caption; selective enhancement not acceptable. Multimedia: MPEG-4 (.mp4) preferred or .mov with H.264; aim for 640×480 or 1280×720, do not exceed 1920×1080; audio .wav/.mp3/.m4a at 160 kb/s; animated GIFs not accepted.

manuscript.titleLimit: Titles should be no more than 96 characters (including spaces).
manuscript.abstractLimit: Research Article abstracts: "125 words or less"; unstructured (no headings) but with prescribed narrative flow — brief background, objectives/methods, results, final sentence of conclusions; no citations or abbreviations in the Abstract; no paragraph breaks in title, author list, or abstract. For Research Articles presented in extended/digital-only format, the print version carries a one-page summary (~500 words in four sections: Introduction, Rationale, Results, Conclusion) plus a summary figure with caption of no more than 65 words.
manuscript.lengthLimits: Research Articles: main text up to 3000 words, plus abstract, 3 to 5 display items (figures or tables), about 50 main-text references. Extended online format (few Research Articles, justified in cover letter): up to 6000 words, up to 6 display items (may include videos), up to 100 main-text references. Reviews: up to 5000 words, up to 150 references, 4 display items; ideally 1-3 authors, no more than 7 without editor permission. Analytical Reviews: up to 6000 words, up to 200 references, 4 to 6 display items. Policy Articles: 2000 to 3000 words, 1 or 2 figures, up to 15 references. Perspectives: ~1000 words (linked to a paper) or ~1800 words (stand-alone), 15 references maximum, 1 figure (or table). Book/Media Reviews: up to 800 words. Policy Forums: 2000 to 3000 words, 1 or 2 figures, up to 15 references. Expert Voices: 1200 words. Letters: up to 300 words; Letters features 200 to 300 words. Editorials: up to 720 words, up to 2 authors. Per-figure caption limit: 200 words. Supplementary materials file: max 50 MB; auxiliary files up to 10 files/25 MB total; movies 50 MB each.
manuscript.requiredSections: Assembly order (initial manuscript, keyed section labels for machine extraction): Title: / Authors: / Affiliations: / Abstract: / Main Text: / References and Notes / Acknowledgments: / List of Supplementary Materials: / Fig. captions (each beginning "Fig. 1" etc.) / Table captions (each beginning "Table 1" etc.), with tables placed after the references. Main Text of Research Articles and Reviews is divided by brief descriptive subheadings (up to 3 levels: bold; bold italic; italic). Materials and Methods go in the supplementary materials (must allow replication); for extended-format articles the methods section runs after the main text. Acknowledgments must contain, in order: non-author contributions, then Funding:, Author contributions: (CRediT encouraged), Diversity/equity/ethics/inclusion [optional], Competing interests: (declare even if none; patent applications disclosed), and Data, code, and materials availability: (all papers need a materials availability statement; if everything is included, state "All data are available in the manuscript or the supplementary materials."). Single combined reference list including supplementary-materials references, numbered continuously. Supplementary materials comprise Materials and Methods, Supplementary Text, figs. S1..., tables S1... (machine-readable csv/tsv/json/xml), data S1 (tabulated data underlying figures, with P values), and multimedia files. Corresponding author marked with *; equal contribution noted with † and the standard sentence "These authors contributed equally to this work" (no co-first/co-senior designations).
manuscript.submissionFormat: Initial: single complete .docx file (Word 2007+/Mac 2011+) with all figures and tables embedded (Word template provided); supplementary materials as one separate .docx or PDF file; LaTeX users must convert to .docx or use the Science LaTeX template and upload a PDF; a combined PDF of manuscript + figures + tables + SM is also required at upload. Spacing: "Use single spacing throughout the text, tables, figure captions, and reference list" (Science asks for single spacing, not double). Line numbers: not stated. Page setup: US letter (8.5 by 11 inches); Times New Roman preferred; avoid Symbol fonts. Revised: collate all text, references, figure legends, and tables into one .docx WITHOUT embedded figures; upload each figure as a separate file (PDF/EPS/AI/TIFF); SM as a separate PDF; equations via MathType or Word's legacy equation editor (not the native Word 2007-2011 editor); ORCID iD required for first and corresponding authors at revision. Cover letter required with stated contents (title + main point, related manuscripts, prior discussions, colleagues who saw the paper, originality statement, consent/animal-care statements, data availability). Submission only online via the Content Tracking System (cts.sciencemag.org); up to 5 suggested and 5 excluded reviewers.

confidence_notes: All content was taken from official science.org pages retrieved 2026-08-13: the three HTML instruction pages were captured in full via a real browser session (science.org blocks plain HTTP fetches with a Cloudflare challenge; a 403 also blocks WebFetch), and the official 'Guide to Preparing Figures' PDF (author_prep_guide_2025.pdf) was downloaded through the browser context and read in full — nothing was paywalled or inferred from third-party sites. Quotes and numbers are verbatim from those pages. Two internal discrepancies on official pages are flagged rather than resolved: (1) column widths — instruction pages say 5.7/12.1/18.4 cm for 1/2/3 columns, while the 2025 figure-guide PDF gives 1 column = 9 cm and 2 column = 18.3 cm; (2) minimum line weight — instruction pages say 0.5 pt at final reduced size, the guide PDF says 0.28 pt (~0.10 mm) at final print size. Also, the info-for-authors page says to use HD 1920x1080 for video 'where possible' while the initial-manuscript page says to aim for 640x480/1280x720 and not exceed 1920x1080. Not stated anywhere on these pages: line numbering, a journal-title abbreviation rule, an author-count truncation rule (full author lists are required; 'et al.' banned), or a maximum line weight. Umbrella-vs-journal scoping: Science is published by AAAS (Nature-family guidelines do not apply); the pages used are specific to the flagship journal Science — sibling journals (Science Advances, Science Signaling, Science Translational Medicine, Science Immunology, Science Robotics) have their own instruction pages with different limits, while the Editorial Policies document is shared across the whole Science family ('editorial policies for Science and the Science family of journals').

citations.inTextMode: numeric-superscript (Nature-family style). Nature Astronomy's own AIP-and-formatting page mandates numbered/numerical citations ("Please use numerical references only for citations" for TeX/LaTeX); the explicit statement that in-text numbers are superscript appears on the Nature-family flagship formatting guide: "When cited in the text, reference numbers are superscript, not in brackets unless they are likely to be confused with a superscript number."
citations.inTextDetails: Nature Astronomy (journal-specific, AIP-and-formatting page): references numbered sequentially in the order they appear in: Main Text, Methods, Data Availability Section, Tables, Figure Legends, Box, Extended Data Figures. Only one publication per reference number. URLs for websites cited parenthetically in the main text, not in the reference list. Unpublished meeting abstracts, papers in preparation, and papers under review/in press without an available preprint must NOT appear in the reference list — mention them in the text with a list of authors (or initials if any are co-authors of the present contribution). Grant details and acknowledgements are not permitted as numbered references. Footnotes are not supported. Methods-only references continue numbering from the last main-text reference and are listed at the end of the paper. Equations referred to as "equation (1)". No collation/range formatting rules are stated on official pages (not stated).
citations.maxReferences: Nature Astronomy content-types page (journal-specific), stated per type: Article — "as a guideline, we typically recommend up to 50 for the main text and another 50 for the Methods section"; Review — "up to 100 (exceptions are possible in special cases)", with short annotations encouraged for particularly important studies (≤10% of all references); Perspective — up to 50; Correspondence — up to 15 (article titles omitted); Comment — up to 15, used sparingly (article titles omitted); Matters Arising — "as a guideline, contributions may have up to 15 references; reference style is as for Articles"; Mission Control — up to 10 in short form (can be omitted entirely); Access Code — up to 10, short form inline. Analysis — as Article.
citations.referenceListFormat: Nature style (examples quoted on Nature Astronomy's own AIP-and-formatting page). Journal article (long-form types — Articles, Letters, Review Articles, Perspectives — REQUIRE article titles): "Eigler, D. M. & Schweizer, E. K. Positioning single atoms with a scanning tunnelling microscope. Nature 344, 524–526 (1990)." Short article types (Comment, News & Views): titles omitted — "Iijima, S. Nature 354, 56–58 (1991)." Book (publisher required): "Jones, R. A. L. Soft Machines: Nanotechnology and Life Ch. 3 (Oxford Univ. Press, 2004)." Dataset/code (must have DOI; include authors, title, publisher/repository name, DOI expressed as full URL): "Hao, Z., AghaKouchak, A., Nakhjiri, N. & Farahmand, A. Global Integrated Drought Monitoring and Prediction System (GIDMaPS) data sets. figshare http://dx.doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.853801 (2014)." Preprint: "Babichev, S. A., Ries, J. & Lvovsky, A. I. Quantum scissors: ... Preprint at https://arXiv.org/quant-ph/0208066 (2002)." Author truncation rule (stated on flagship Nature formatting guide, not restated on Nature Astronomy pages): "All authors should be included in reference lists unless there are more than five, in which case only the first author should be given, followed by 'et al.'"; authors listed surname first, comma, then initials. Typography (flagship guide): article titles upright (not italic), first word capitalized, ending with a full stop; book titles italic with main words capitalized; journal titles italic and abbreviated according to common usage; volume numbers bold; publisher and city required for books.

figures.widths: Nature-branded research journals "Guide to preparing final artwork" PDF (linked from Nature Astronomy's AIP-and-formatting page): original research and review content — 1-column width 88 mm, 2-column width 180 mm; maximum figure height depends on caption length: caption <300 words: ~130 mm (1-column) / ~185 mm (2-column); <150 words: ~180 mm / ~210 mm; <50 words: ~220 mm / ~225 mm. All other content: 1-column 58 mm, 2-column 121 mm, 3-column 185 mm. Nature Astronomy AIP page itself: "Figure panels should be... saved at a maximum width of 180 mm." (The separate Nature research figure guide site quotes flagship-Nature print widths of 89 mm / 183 mm with 170 mm maximum height; for Nature Astronomy the 88/180 mm branded-journals figures govern.) Extended Data: maximum page dimensions 180 mm wide x 170 mm tall, must fit a single page with legend.
figures.fonts: Sans-serif typeface required, "preferably Helvetica or Arial". Maximum text size 7 pt, minimum text size 5 pt at final size (final artwork guide + research figure guide). Nature Astronomy AIP page: "Use a 5–7 pt san serif font for standard text labelling and Symbol font for Greek characters." Amino-acid sequences in Courier (or other monospaced) one-letter code in lines of 50 or 100 characters. Do not outline text; embed fonts (TrueType 2 or 42); text must remain editable (e.g., Matplotlib.rcParams['pdf.fonttype']=42 for Python).
figures.lineWeights: "Lines and strokes should be set between 0.25 and 1 pt" — stated on the Nature research figure guide (Extended data formatting guidelines page: "Our line range is between 0.25 pt and 1 pt"). Not stated on Nature Astronomy's own journal pages.
figures.color: Final artwork guide: original research content supplied in RGB colour mode; all other content (including Perspectives, Progress Articles and Review Articles) supplied in CMYK. Research figure guide: RGB recommended (wider gamut; auto-converted to CMYK for print). Accessibility (research figure guide, applies across Nature journals): an accessible colour palette is required — the guide reproduces the Wong colour-blind-safe palette (Wong, B. Nature Methods 8, 441 (2011)) with 8 named colours and hex/RGB/CMYK values (Black #000000, Orange #e69f00, Sky blue #56b4e9, Bluish green #009e73, Yellow #f0e442, Blue #0072b2, Vermillion #d55e00, Reddish purple #cc79a7); avoid red/green combinations and rainbow scales; nature.com adheres to WCAG 2.1 level AA wherever possible; text contrast ratio >4.5; avoid coloured text (black/white text on high-contrast background); avoid patterns, gridlines, drop shadows, decorative icons. Colour charges: Nature Astronomy AIP page says charges apply "for authors of primary subscription content who wish to publish figures in colour in Nature Portfolio print journals" (print journals only).
figures.formats: Main figures: vector files with editable layers required for graphs/charts/schematics/line art — preferred .ai, .eps, .pdf (retain editing capabilities); acceptable: layered Photoshop, PowerPoint (saved to PDF), plain .svg, Excel, .ps; NOT accepted for main-figure vector art: .jpeg, .tiff, .png, Canvas, DeltaGraph, Tex, ChemDraw, SigmaPlot, CorelDraw. Photographs/complex illustrations as bitmaps at minimum 300 dpi (Nature Astronomy AIP: "minimum resolution of 300 dpi"); research figure guide adds maximum online-proof resolution 450 dpi, so ≥450 dpi ensures best quality; do not artificially upsample. Keep each final figure ≤50 MB. Extended Data figures: .jpeg (preferred), .tiff or .eps only, RGB, maximum 300 dpi, file ≤10 MB, named CorrespondingAuthorSurname_EDfig1.jpg. Initial submission (Nature Astronomy): no special formatting; PDF, Word or TeX/LaTeX accepted (compiled PDFs for LaTeX); Matters Arising figures at submission "ideally as JPEGs".
figures.panelLabels: Research figure guide (Nature-family): "Separate panels in multi-panelled figures should be labelled with 8-pt bold, upright (not italic) and lowercase a, b, c, etc." Panels arranged in alphabetical order, minimizing white space. Figures cited in sequence in the main text as "Fig. 1, Fig. 2" (Nature Astronomy AIP page). Not restated on Nature Astronomy's own pages beyond the citation form.
figures.other: Do not flatten labels or scale/error bars onto images (a stated common cause of delay); keep them on separate editable layers. Use scale bars, not magnification factors; include error bars where appropriate. Figure legends: brief title plus short description of each panel cited in sequence; avoid methodological detail; use verbal cues ("open red triangles") not symbols; describe centre values (median/average), how error bars were calculated, sample size (n), statistical test used and P values; legend must not exceed the article-type word limit (Nature Astronomy AIP; flagship Nature states legends <300 words each). Stereo images: present for divergent wall-eyed viewing with panels separated by ~5.5 cm, submitted at final size. Extended Data: max 10 items, not copy-edited/styled by the journal, each must fit a single PDF page and be cited discretely in the main text. Chemical structures via ChemDraw journal template, final files at 100% as .cdx. Generative-AI images (DALL-E, Stable Diffusion, Midjourney) not permitted for cover artwork. Authors responsible for copyright permissions, incl. BioRender licence confirmation.

manuscript.titleLimit: Not stated on Nature Astronomy's own pages. (Nature-family flagship guide, applying to Nature itself: titles do not exceed two lines in print = 75 characters including spaces, and do not normally include numbers, acronyms, abbreviations or punctuation — Nature Astronomy does not restate this.) Journal-specific heading limits: Analysis section headings "must be fewer than 60 characters including spaces"; Article subheadings for Results/Methods required, none in Discussion.
manuscript.abstractLimit: Article: "up to 200 words, unreferenced" (Nature Astronomy content-types page). Analysis: follows Article formatting. Matters Arising: no formal abstract — contributions start with "a brief paragraph that summarizes the message of the article without specialized terminology... used as the abstract for submission purposes." Review, Perspective, Comment, others: abstract limit not stated. All abstracts are unstructured.
manuscript.lengthLimits: Per Nature Astronomy content-types page: Article — main text (introduction/results/discussion) up to 3,000 words excluding abstract, Methods, references and figure captions; up to 6 display items (figures and/or tables) in main text plus up to 10 Extended Data items (each cited from main text). Analysis — as Article, in 4–6 topically headed sections ending with "Conclusions". Review — main text 3,000–4,000 words, up to 100 references. Perspective — up to 3,000 words, up to 50 references. Correspondence — 300–800 words, 1 display item, up to 15 references. Comment — typically 1–3 pages, up to 15 references. Feature — up to 3,000 words. Mission Control — single typeset page, typically up to 650 words, one figure (landscape preferred). Access Code — single typeset page, typically up to 800 words, one code snippet. Matters Arising — "as concise as possible, and ideally not exceed 1,200 words", one or two small figures/tables, up to 3 Extended Data items.
manuscript.requiredSections: Article (journal-specific): main text divided as Introduction (without heading), Results, Discussion, Methods; Results and Methods divided by topical subheadings, Discussion without subheadings. Methods subdivided by short bold headings (subsections such as Statistics encouraged); Methods-only references listed at end. Reference numbering order implies overall ordering: Main Text, Methods, Data Availability Section, Tables, Figure Legends, Box, Extended Data Figures. A data availability statement is mandatory for all original research (Nature Portfolio policy on the Nature Astronomy reporting-standards page: "All published manuscripts reporting original research in Nature Portfolio journals must include a data availability statement"); datasets in repositories must be formally cited in the reference list. Acknowledgements brief; separate funding statement with stated format ("A.B.C. discloses support for the research of this work from Funder [grant number xxxx]..."). Author contributions and competing interests statements required (stated explicitly for Matters Arising; per editorial policies generally). Tables at end of the text document. Extended Data legends in an 'Inventory of Supporting Information' document.
manuscript.submissionFormat: Initial submission (journal-specific page): "Your initial submission does not need to be specially formatted"; accepted formats PDF, Word or TeX/LaTeX (submit compiled PDFs if using TeX/LaTeX). Submission must include manuscript file (with Methods, figures, Extended Data if applicable), cover letter, and optional Supplementary Information. Double spacing and line numbers: NOT stated on Nature Astronomy pages (the flagship Nature guide asks for double-spaced text with line numbers, but that is Nature-specific). After Acceptance in Principle (AIP): Word or TeX/LaTeX only — "We do not accept PDFs for final submissions"; Word: Symbol font for Greek characters; LaTeX: standard class files (article.cls, revtex.cls, amsart.cls), single .tex file in default Computer Modern fonts, no personal macros, graphicx.sty recommended, BibTeX output pasted from .bbl into the .tex with \bibliography commands deleted, file must compile with no errors/warnings. Supplementary Information as a single combined PDF (complex tables/data as Excel or .csv); supplementary software as .zip or .tar archive. ORCID must be linked before final acceptance.

Journal-specific numbers (word limits, abstract 200 words, display items, reference counts, 300 dpi / 180 mm / 5–7 pt figure specs, reference examples) come verbatim from Nature Astronomy's own pages. Umbrella attribution: the 'Guide to preparing final artwork' PDF (Nature-branded research journals) is linked from Nature Astronomy's AIP page, so its 88/180 mm widths and RGB/CMYK rules apply to the journal; the research-figure-guide.nature.com site is the Nature-family figure guide (line weights 0.25–1 pt, 8-pt bold lowercase panel labels, Wong accessibility palette) and is linked from the flagship formatting guide — Nature Astronomy links the same artwork ecosystem but does not restate those numbers itself. Items marked flagship-only (75-char title, superscript citation statement, >5-author et al. rule, double spacing + line numbers, legend <300 words) appear only on nature.com/nature/for-authors/formatting-guide; Nature Astronomy's own initial-formatting page explicitly says no special formatting is needed and states no title limit, spacing or line-number requirement. Minor discrepancy noted between umbrella documents: figure widths 88/180 mm (branded-journals artwork PDF) vs 89/183 mm (figure-guide site, flagship Nature sizes). Nothing was paywalled or unreachable. AAAS guidelines are irrelevant here (AAAS publishes Science; Nature Astronomy is Springer Nature / Nature Portfolio)."
